My go-to transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, is releasing another major update today, adding real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and a new transcription model. Here's what's new.

MacWhisper deepens its Apple Intelligence integration

I've mentioned many times before how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially for my podcast workflow.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest Mac AI transcription tools. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has been continuously improved, expanding support for new models, services, and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, watched folders, system-level dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, n8n, and more.

Today MacWhisper is releasing version 15.2, introducing more powerful speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced only hours ago.

Another highlight of today's update: real-time meeting transcription.

This feature has been at the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap and has finally arrived, allowing users to view, search, copy, or send live transcription text while a meeting is in progress.

On the actual transcription model side, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model on top of the existing foundation, supporting 22 languages, and further strengthens integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users now running macOS (including EU versions) can search transcription content system-wide, open it with Siri, pull text into Shortcuts, and reference on-screen transcription content in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folder and subfolder functionality to help organize transcription files and meeting notes, and also supports dragging existing transcription files into folders from the sidebar.
